inputs.original_text: Health workers took their opposition to proposed reform bills to Unity Fountain in Maitama on Thursday, but street pressure should not dictate national policy. The National Assembly must judge the bills on their merits and put patients and the country’s long-term welfare ahead of union interests. A strained health sector needs responsible reform, not the preservation of arrangements simply because powerful groups resist change.
inputs.modified_text: Health workers took their opposition to the proposed reform bills to Unity Fountain in Maitama on Thursday, and that protest should be heard as more than “union interests.” The people who keep a strained health sector running have a direct stake in whether reforms protect patients and working conditions—or deepen existing failures. The National Assembly should scrutinize the bills on their merits, but that means listening to frontline workers, not treating public pressure as a reason to dismiss them. Reform should strengthen care for everyone, especially those least able to absorb the cost of a broken system.
